model_under_review: CNN causal–LSTM unidirectional–learned-query content attention; sqrt(A)+a_tr*(1e-4+softplus(z)); normalized MSE; 1210 parameters

source_records.title: Sample-Specific Output Constraints for Neural Networks
source_records.verified_locator: Printed p.6816, Supported Constraints and Generalizations, final bullet; guard phi(z,s)=exp(z)+b. Method fig.1 and Eqs.(3)-(4).
source_records.source_mechanism: Differentiable sample-dependent output guard; constraint descriptor also enters learned network.
source_records.source_target: Facial landmark regression and vehicle follow-object control.
source_records.current_E3_overlap: A positive learned excess added to a sample-specific lower bound.
source_records.current_E3_difference: E3 uses b=sqrt(A)+1e-4*a_tr and a_tr*softplus(z), with A derived from six observed returns. It does not implement the full arbitrary-constraint architecture.
source_records.R1_consequence: The broad floor-plus-positive-excess mechanism is already explicit. The particular bound and softplus substitution do not establish a substantive adaptation by themselves.
source_records.limits: No exact E3 target or training recipe identified here. This conceptual antecedent does not prove historical copying or universal nonnovelty.

source_records.title: Lipschitz Normalization for Self-Attention Layers with Application to Graph Neural Networks
source_records.verified_locator: §3.3 Eq.(2), PDF p.3; §5 Eqs.(17)-(18), PDF p.5; sentence after Eq.(17) states Q is a model parameter.
source_records.source_mechanism: Softmax pooling with linear query scores and LipschitzNorm score normalization.
source_records.source_target: Graph neural network and graph Transformer tasks.
source_records.current_E3_overlap: Softmax pooling and a learned query independent of the input at inference.
source_records.current_E3_difference: E3 bounds parameters and latent states but does not implement the LipschitzNorm denominator of Eq.(17).
source_records.R1_consequence: A learned query and weighted attention pooling are not sufficient novelty claims. A genuinely modified propagation rule would need its own comparison.
source_records.limits: The graph depth instability is not established as a defect of the shallow E3 encoder.

source_records.title: Effective Approaches to Attention-based Neural Machine Translation
source_records.verified_locator: §3.1, printed p.1414, Eqs.(7)-(8), Fig.2 and paragraph defining weighted context.
source_records.source_mechanism: Content alignment over recurrent encoder hidden states.
source_records.current_E3_overlap: Attention over recurrent hidden states and a weighted context vector.
source_records.current_E3_difference: The paper queries with the current decoder state; E3 has a learned vector shared across samples and uses a scalar volatility head.
source_records.R1_consequence: Recurrent content attention has clear antecedents; the shared query is covered more closely by P02.
source_records.limits: No CNN, sigma7 target or observable-floor head is asserted in this source.

source_records.title: The Lipschitz Constant of Self-Attention
source_records.verified_locator: §3 Theorem 3.1; §6 Conclusion and Discussion, PDF p.8, paragraph beginning the bounded-input alternative.
source_records.source_mechanism: Non-Lipschitz standard dot-product attention on unbounded domains; Lipschitz L2 attention; discussion of compact inputs.
source_records.source_target: Attention analysis and character-level language modelling.
source_records.current_E3_overlap: Analysis of attention regularity under an explicitly bounded latent domain.
source_records.current_E3_difference: E3 proves a conditional bound for its scalar head with fixed parameters and fixed floor, not the paper’s L2 attention or a bound from raw OHLCV.
source_records.R1_consequence: Having a bound on a compact latent domain is technical evidence, not by itself a new mechanism or raw-input robustness guarantee.
source_records.limits: No transfer of the L2-attention theorem to E3. All hypothesis domains must remain explicit.

source_records.title: TimeMixer: Decomposable Multiscale Mixing for Time Series Forecasting
source_records.verified_locator: §3.1–3.3 (multiscale architecture, PDM and FMM); Appendix J.
source_records.source_mechanism: Past Decomposable Mixing and Future Multipredictor Mixing across scales.
source_records.current_E3_overlap: A forecasting task and benchmark role; no identity of core mechanism.
source_records.current_E3_difference: E3 uses CNN–LSTM content pooling and a lower-bound readout, rather than PDM/FMM.
source_records.R1_consequence: Being different from the guide paper does not establish novelty against the family E3 actually uses.
source_records.limits: A measured ETTh1 calendar-adapter limitation is not automatically a sigma7 BTC limitation corrected by E3.

source_records.title: HARNet: A Convolutional Neural Network for Realized Volatility Forecasting
source_records.source_mechanism: Causal dilated convolutions initialized to reproduce a HAR baseline; loss-specific optimization analysis.
source_records.current_E3_overlap: Neural volatility forecasting with explicit domain structure and causal filters.
source_records.current_E3_difference: E3 uses a short centered-return volatility target and an additive output guard; it does not use the HAR initialization or filters.
source_records.R1_consequence: Causal convolution and incorporating financial structure into a network are established. A new adaptation must specify what beyond that is changed.
source_records.limits: RV, sigma7 and their loss functions are different estimands; reported errors are not directly comparable.

source_records.title: Forecasting Bitcoin volatility using machine learning techniques
source_records.verified_locator: Institutional Abstract and bibliographic metadata. Reading PDF returns Anubis Access Denied; Birmingham linked PDF returns 403.
source_records.source_mechanism: LSTM and hybrid CNN–LSTM; abstract describes Markov Transition Field integration.
source_records.source_target: Bitcoin volatility with 1-day to 2-month horizons, as stated in abstract.
source_records.current_E3_difference: The accessible abstract does not establish equality to population-centered sigma7, the E3 attention rule or its floor readout.
source_records.R1_consequence: Generic CNN–LSTM Bitcoin volatility novelty is weakened, while exact-target equivalence remains unverified.
source_records.limits: No equations, complete architecture, training setup or numerical superiority are inferred from the unavailable body.

source_records.title: Attention-based CNN–LSTM for high-frequency multiple cryptocurrency trend prediction
source_records.verified_locator: Publisher title, abstract and author preview from indexed primary ScienceDirect result. Direct full page returned 403.
source_records.source_mechanism: Attention-based CNN–LSTM exploiting multiple frequencies and currencies.
source_records.current_E3_overlap: CNN–LSTM with attention in cryptocurrency applications.
source_records.current_E3_difference: Trend classification differs from centered rolling sigma7 regression; exact readout and loss cannot be checked from the observed extract.
source_records.R1_consequence: The architecture’s name and use in crypto are not original by themselves; this is not proof of the same phenomenon/task.
source_records.limits: Body not read; no equivalence of equations, support constraint or parameter count is asserted.

source_records.title: Probabilistic Forecasting Cryptocurrencies Volatility: From Point to Quantile Forecasts
source_records.source_mechanism: QRS residual simulation, quantile linear regression and quantile regression forests over point forecasts.
source_records.source_target: Next-day daily BTC realized variance from 288 intraday five-minute returns; 99 conditional quantiles.
source_records.current_E3_overlap: Probabilistic uncertainty for crypto volatility; baseline LSTM and MLP are included.
source_records.current_E3_difference: E3 is a point model of centered rolling seven-return sigma, with a deterministic sample-dependent floor. The paper’s quantiles are a separate meta-forecasting layer.
source_records.R1_consequence: Adding quantiles or probabilistic forecasts in crypto is not by itself new; a future law-based head needs a much narrower algorithmic distinction.
source_records.limits: Preprint v1; no exact finite-atom U-to-sigma pushforward mechanism is identified in the examined sections. That absence is bounded, not global.

source_records.authors: Yang, Lorch, Graule, Lakkaraju and Doshi-Velez
source_records.title: Incorporating Interpretable Output Constraints in Bayesian Neural Networks
source_records.verified_locator: §4 Definitions 4.1–4.3, Eqs.(1)–(2); §4.1 conditional output-constrained priors; §4.2 approximate inference.
source_records.source_mechanism: Deterministic/probabilistic output constraints induced through Bayesian output-constrained priors.
source_records.source_target: Low-dimensional simulations, clinical action, recidivism and credit prediction.
source_records.current_E3_overlap: Input-dependent admissible output sets and constraints on predictive distributions.
source_records.current_E3_difference: E3 uses an architectural point-output guard with a deterministic lower bound; it has no weight posterior or COCP inference.
source_records.R1_consequence: Output-support knowledge and probabilistic output constraints are established; the broad phrase support-aware probabilistic network cannot sustain novelty alone.
source_records.limits: Soft approximate posterior constraint satisfaction is not equated with E3’s architectural hard inequality. A proposed new head must specify its distinct rule.
